summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with refractory multiple myeloma, COPD, and a history of bladder cancer with neobladder, was admitted from clinic with shortness of breath and hypoxia. He had recently received Cytoxan chemotherapy and presented with fatigue and malaise. A nasal swab confirmed RSV infection, and imaging showed reticular opacities consistent with viral pneumonia. He was treated with three doses of IVIG and continued on azithromycin for community-acquired pneumonia. His respiratory status improved, and he experienced transient delirium that resolved. He was counseled on smoking cessation and started on a nicotine patch. Revlimid and Bactrim were held due to immunosuppression. He was discharged home on oxygen with physical therapy support and instructions to follow up with his oncologist.
problems: Multiple myeloma, without mention of having achieved remission
Peripheral stem cells replaced by transplant
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of bladder
